questions.stem: Which of the following is a common source of electric shock in an electronics workshop?
options: Working on a live chassis while standing on a wet floor
Switching off the mains before work
questions.explanation: A wet floor provides a path to earth through the body; rubber soles, isolation transformers and switching off reduce risk.

questions.topic: Safety Checks in Servicing Radio Receiver
questions.stem: Before touching components in the power supply section of a mains radio that has just been switched off, the technician should
options: touch the capacitor terminals with both hands
increase the volume to drain the power
discharge the large filter capacitors through a suitable resistor
spray water on the board to cool it
questions.explanation: Filter capacitors can hold a dangerous charge after switch-off; discharging through a resistor is safe.

questions.stem: The final anode of a CRT television picture tube may hold a dangerous charge long after switch-off because
options: the deflection coils store chemical energy
the screen phosphor generates electricity in darkness
the tube acts as a high-voltage capacitor charged to many kilovolts by the EHT supply
questions.explanation: The aquadag coatings form a capacitor charged to the EHT (tens of kilovolts); it must be discharged to chassis with an insulated lead.

questions.stem: Silicon and germanium are classified as
questions.explanation: Their conductivity lies between that of conductors and insulators and can be controlled by doping.

questions.stem: According to the law of electric charges,
options: like charges attract and unlike charges repel
charges have no effect on one another
like charges repel and unlike charges attract
questions.explanation: Two positive or two negative charges repel; a positive and a negative attract.

questions.stem: A ceramic capacitor is marked "104". Its value is
questions.explanation: The code means 10 followed by 4 zeros pF = 100,000 pF = 100 nF = 0.1 microfarad.

questions.stem: A resistor with colour bands brown, black, orange and gold has a value of
questions.explanation: Brown = 1, black = 0, orange multiplier = x1000: 10 x 1000 = 10 kilohms; gold = 5%.

questions.stem: A current of 3.5 A enters a junction. One branch leaving the junction carries 1.2 A. The current in the only other branch is
questions.explanation: By Kirchhoff's current law, current in = current out: 3.5 - 1.2 = 2.3 A.

questions.stem: The transistor configuration with a voltage gain of about one, high input impedance and low output impedance, used as a buffer, is the
questions.explanation: The emitter follower gives current gain but unity voltage gain; common emitter gives high voltage gain with phase inversion.

questions.stem: A zinc-carbon torch cell that cannot be recharged is an example of a
questions.explanation: Primary cells are used once and discarded; secondary cells such as lead-acid can be recharged.

questions.stem: Resistors of 1 kilohm and 2 kilohms are connected in parallel across a 9 V battery. The total current is
A current of 0.5 A flows through a 40 ohm resistor. The power dissipated is
questions.explanation: P = I^2 R = 0.25 x 40 = 10 W; I x R gives the voltage (20 V), not power.

questions.stem: On an oscilloscope, a sine wave measures 20 V peak-to-peak and one cycle occupies 4 ms. Its r.m.s. voltage and frequency are
The braided copper strip used with a soldering iron to soak up molten solder from a joint is the
questions.explanation: Solder wick draws molten solder up by capillary action; a sucker uses suction.

questions.stem: When an analogue ohmmeter is used to test a good silicon diode, it shows
options: low resistance one way and high resistance when the leads are reversed
the same medium resistance both ways
questions.explanation: A good diode conducts in forward bias only; zero both ways means shorted and infinite both ways means open.

questions.stem: The instrument that indicates whether a point in a digital circuit is at logic HIGH, logic LOW or pulsing is the
questions.explanation: A logic probe uses LEDs to show logic states and pulses; a signal tracer follows audio/RF signals.

questions.topic: Concept of Emission and Photoelectric Devices
questions.stem: The release of electrons from the heated cathode of a cathode ray tube is called
questions.explanation: Heat gives electrons enough energy to escape the cathode surface; photoelectric emission uses light.

questions.stem: An n-type semiconductor is produced by doping pure silicon with
options: a pentavalent impurity such as phosphorus
a trivalent impurity such as boron
questions.explanation: Five-valence-electron impurities donate free electrons, giving n-type material; trivalent impurities give p-type.

questions.stem: In a d.c. power supply unit, the stage that follows the rectifier and smooths the pulsating d.c. is the
questions.explanation: Order: transformer, rectifier, filter, regulator; the filter capacitor reduces ripple.

questions.stem: A Class B push-pull output stage is often biased slightly into Class AB in order to
questions.explanation: In pure Class B each transistor is off near zero crossing, causing crossover distortion; a small bias current removes it.

questions.stem: Applying NEGATIVE feedback to an amplifier
options: reduces gain but increases bandwidth and reduces distortion
questions.explanation: Negative feedback trades gain for stability, wider bandwidth and lower distortion and noise; positive feedback can cause oscillation.

questions.stem: A multivibrator that has NO stable state and continuously produces square waves is the
options: Schmitt trigger with one stable state
questions.explanation: The astable is free-running; the monostable has one stable state (one-shot) and the bistable two (flip-flop).

questions.topic: Electronic Communication Systems (Block Diagram and Noise)
questions.stem: Noise generated by the random motion of electrons in resistors and conductors is called
questions.explanation: Thermal noise is internal and rises with temperature and bandwidth; atmospheric and man-made noise are external.

questions.stem: FM radio broadcasting in Nigeria (88 to 108 MHz) takes place in the
questions.explanation: VHF covers 30 to 300 MHz; MF (300 kHz to 3 MHz) carries AM medium-wave broadcasting.

questions.stem: A microphone is a transducer that converts
questions.explanation: The microphone is an input transducer; the loudspeaker does the reverse.

questions.stem: The envelope of an AM wave has a maximum amplitude of 15 V and a minimum amplitude of 5 V. The percentage modulation is
questions.explanation: m = (Vmax - Vmin)/(Vmax + Vmin) = 10/20 = 0.5 = 50%.

questions.stem: The ability of a radio receiver to pick out the wanted station and reject stations on nearby frequencies is its
questions.explanation: Selectivity rejects adjacent signals; sensitivity is the ability to receive weak signals.

questions.stem: A tuned circuit resonates at 600 kHz and has a Q-factor of 40. Its bandwidth is
questions.explanation: Bandwidth = f0 / Q = 600 / 40 = 15 kHz.

questions.stem: Communication satellites that appear fixed above one point on the equator orbit at a height of about
questions.explanation: Geostationary orbit is about 35,786 km above the equator, where the period equals one day.

questions.stem: In an analogue PAL television transmitter of the type used in Nigeria, the picture and sound signals are
options: picture amplitude-modulated and sound frequency-modulated on separate carriers
questions.explanation: The video carrier is AM (vestigial sideband) and the sound carrier is FM, a few megahertz above it.

questions.topic: Image and Sound Reproduction in TV Receiver
questions.stem: In the 625-line PAL system, each picture (frame) is built up from two interlaced fields, and the number of fields per second is
questions.explanation: There are 25 frames per second, each of two fields, giving 50 fields per second (and 15,625 lines per second).

questions.stem: A black-and-white TV shows only a bright horizontal line across the middle of the screen, while sound is normal. The fault is in the
questions.explanation: Without vertical scanning the beam traces only one horizontal line; a vertical line would indicate a horizontal deflection fault.

questions.topic: Principle of Colour Signal, Transmission and Reception
questions.stem: The three primary colours used in colour television are
questions.explanation: Television uses additive mixing of red, green and blue light.

questions.topic: Principles of Operation of Colour Television Receiver
questions.stem: In a PAL colour television receiver, the stage that switches off the colour circuits when a black-and-white transmission is received is the
questions.explanation: The colour killer prevents coloured noise appearing on a monochrome picture when no colour burst is received.

questions.topic: Soldering and Desoldering in Electronic Circuits
questions.stem: When soldering a transistor into a circuit board, a pair of long-nose pliers gripping its lead acts as a
options: heat sink to protect the transistor from overheating
questions.explanation: The pliers conduct heat away from the junction so the device is not damaged.

questions.topic: Fault Finding and Repairs in Radio Receiver
questions.stem: A mains radio produces a loud 100 Hz hum in the loudspeaker. The most likely faulty component is the
options: dried-out filter capacitor in the power supply
questions.explanation: A failed reservoir/filter capacitor leaves large ripple at twice mains frequency (full-wave), heard as hum.

questions.topic: Diagnosis and Repair of Black and White TV Receiver
questions.stem: Sound is present on a monochrome TV but there is no raster (screen completely dark). The section to check first is the
options: line output/EHT stage and the CRT heater supply
questions.explanation: No light at all means no EHT or no CRT heater; since sound works, the common power supply is probably good.

questions.topic: Diagnosis and Repair of a Colour Television Receiver
questions.stem: The instrument that produces a standard pattern of coloured vertical stripes used to check and adjust a colour TV is the
questions.explanation: Colour bar patterns show whether each colour and its saturation are reproduced correctly.

questions.stem: The document a repair shop fills when receiving a customer's faulty television, recording the fault, date and estimated cost, is the
questions.explanation: The repair order (job card) is the record and receipt for equipment left for repair.

questions.topic: Business Opportunities in Radio, TV and Electronics Works
questions.stem: Which of the following is a business opportunity open to a trained radio and television technician?
questions.explanation: Installing satellite TV systems, antennas and repairing electronics are direct openings for RTV graduates.

questions.stem:
A 100 ohm resistor, a 0.1 H inductor and a 10 microfarad capacitor are connected in series across a 12 V, 50 Hz supply.
(a) Calculate (i) the inductive reactance (ii) the capacitive reactance (iii) the impedance (iv) the current. [8 marks]
(b) Calculate the resonant frequency of the circuit. [3 marks]
(c) State whether the circuit is inductive or capacitive at 50 Hz, giving a reason. [2 marks]
(d) What happens to the current at resonance? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a)(i) X_L = 2 x pi x f x L = 2 x 3.142 x 50 x 0.1 = 31.4 ohms
2 marks: (a)(ii) X_C = 1/(2 x pi x f x C) = 1/(2 x 3.142 x 50 x 10 x 10^-6) = 318.3 ohms
2 marks: (a)(iii) Z = sqrt(R^2 + (X_C - X_L)^2) = sqrt(100^2 + 286.9^2) = 303.8 ohms
2 marks: (a)(iv) I = V/Z = 12/303.8 = 0.0395 A (about 39.5 mA)
3 marks: (b) f0 = 1/(2 x pi x sqrt(LC)) = 1/(2 x 3.142 x sqrt(0.1 x 10 x 10^-6)) = 159.2 Hz
2 marks: (c) Capacitive, because X_C is greater than X_L at 50 Hz (current leads the voltage)
2 marks: (d) At resonance X_L = X_C, impedance is minimum (= R) so the current is maximum (12/100 = 0.12 A) and in phase with the voltage
questions.explanation: X_L = 31.4 ohms, X_C = 318.3 ohms, Z = 303.8 ohms, I = 39.5 mA. f0 = 159.2 Hz. At 50 Hz the circuit is capacitive (X_C > X_L). At resonance the current is maximum, 0.12 A, in phase with V.

questions.stem:
(a) List in order the stages of an AM superheterodyne receiver from aerial to loudspeaker. [7 marks]
(b) State the function of (i) the mixer (ii) the local oscillator (iii) the IF amplifier (iv) the detector. [4 marks]
(c) State two advantages of the superheterodyne receiver over the tuned radio frequency (TRF) receiver. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
7 marks: (a) 1 mark each in correct order: aerial; RF amplifier/tuner; mixer (frequency changer); local oscillator (feeding mixer); IF amplifier; detector (demodulator) with AGC; AF amplifier driving loudspeaker
1 mark: (b)(i) Mixer: combines the incoming RF and local oscillator signals to produce the intermediate frequency
1 mark: (b)(ii) Local oscillator: generates a frequency higher than the signal by the IF (e.g. 455 kHz) and tracks the tuning
1 mark: (b)(iii) IF amplifier: provides most of the gain and selectivity at a fixed frequency
1 mark: (b)(iv) Detector: recovers the audio signal from the IF (demodulation) and supplies AGC voltage
4 marks: (c) Any two, 2 marks each: better selectivity; higher sensitivity/gain; uniform performance across the band because amplification is at a fixed IF; easier and more stable tuning
questions.explanation: Aerial, RF stage, mixer with local oscillator, IF amplifier, detector, AF amplifier, loudspeaker. The mixer produces the IF, the oscillator runs at signal + IF, the IF amplifier gives gain and selectivity, the detector recovers audio. The superhet has better selectivity, sensitivity and uniform performance than the TRF.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between direct current and alternating current. [4 marks]
(b) State two uses of each. [4 marks]
(c) An alternating voltage has a peak value of 170 V and a frequency of 60 Hz. Calculate (i) its r.m.s. value (ii) its average value over a half-cycle (iii) its periodic time. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Direct current flows in one direction only with constant (or unidirectional) magnitude, e.g. from a battery
2 marks: (a) Alternating current reverses direction periodically and its magnitude varies, usually sinusoidally, e.g. from the mains
2 marks: (b) D.C., any two: charging batteries; electronic circuits/radios; electroplating; torches; vehicle electrical systems
2 marks: (b) A.C., any two: domestic mains supply; electric motors; transformers/power transmission; heating and lighting
3 marks: (c)(i) V_rms = 0.707 x 170 = 120.2 V
2 marks: (c)(ii) V_av = 0.637 x 170 = 108.3 V
2 marks: (c)(iii) T = 1/f = 1/60 = 0.0167 s (16.7 ms)
questions.explanation: D.C. flows one way (battery); a.c. reverses periodically (mains). D.C. for batteries and electronics; a.c. for mains, motors and transformers. V_rms = 120.2 V, V_av = 108.3 V, T = 16.7 ms.

questions.stem:
(a) Draw up, in words, the block arrangement of a regulated d.c. power supply unit and state the function of each block. [8 marks]
(b) A radio power supply gives no output voltage. Describe four checks you would make to locate the fault. [4 marks]
(c) State three precautions when dismantling the power supply of a radio set. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Transformer: steps the mains voltage down to the required level and isolates the circuit
2 marks: (a) Rectifier: converts a.c. to pulsating d.c. (diode bridge/half-wave)
2 marks: (a) Filter: smooths the pulsating d.c. using reservoir capacitor (and choke/resistor)
2 marks: (a) Regulator/stabiliser: keeps the output voltage constant despite load or mains changes (zener or IC regulator)
4 marks: (b) Any four, 1 mark each: check mains supply, plug and fuse; check transformer primary and secondary continuity/voltage; test rectifier diodes with ohmmeter; check filter capacitor for short/open; check regulator input and output voltages; check for shorted load
3 marks: (c) Any three, 1 mark each: disconnect from mains; discharge capacitors; note/label wire positions before removal; use correct tools; avoid overheating components when desoldering; keep screws and parts orderly
questions.explanation: Transformer (step down), rectifier (a.c. to d.c.), filter (smoothing), regulator (constant output). For no output: check mains and fuse, transformer windings, diodes, capacitor, regulator and load. Precautions: unplug, discharge capacitors, label wires, use correct tools, avoid overheating.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe how a multimeter is used to measure (i) the d.c. voltage across a resistor in a working circuit (ii) the current through it (iii) the resistance of the resistor. [9 marks]
(b) State four precautions to take when using a multimeter. [4 marks]
(c) State two advantages of a digital multimeter over an analogue multimeter. [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Select d.c. volts on a range above the expected value (1); connect the meter in parallel across the resistor (1); red probe to the more positive end, black to the negative, and read (1)
3 marks: (a)(ii) Switch off, break the circuit at one end of the resistor (1); select d.c. current range and insert the meter in series (1); observe polarity, switch on and read (1)
3 marks: (a)(iii) Switch off and disconnect at least one end of the resistor from the circuit (1); select ohms range and zero the meter (analogue) (1); connect probes across the resistor and read, multiplying by the range factor (1)
4 marks: (b) Any four, 1 mark each: start on highest range; never measure resistance in a live circuit; never connect an ammeter in parallel; observe polarity; select correct function before connecting; switch off/to a.c. volts after use; check battery and probes
2 marks: (c) Any two, 1 mark each: no parallax error/easy to read; higher accuracy; high input impedance causing little loading; auto-ranging and polarity indication
questions.explanation: Volts: parallel, correct range and polarity. Current: break circuit, meter in series. Resistance: power off, isolate the resistor, zero and measure. Precautions: highest range first, no ohms on live circuits, no ammeter in parallel, observe polarity. Digital meters are easier to read, more accurate and load circuits less.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain why good customer relations are important to a radio and TV repair business. [4 marks]
(b) State four rules of telephone courtesy for a technician answering business calls. [4 marks]
(c) Describe how a technician should handle a customer who complains that a repaired television has developed the same fault again. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Any two, 2 marks each: retains customers and brings repeat business; customers recommend the shop to others; builds trust and reputation; reduces complaints and disputes
4 marks: (b) Any four, 1 mark each: answer promptly and greet politely; identify yourself and the business; speak clearly and listen attentively; take accurate messages/notes; avoid eating or shouting; end the call politely and follow up
7 marks: (c) 1 mark each: listen calmly without arguing; apologise for the inconvenience; check the repair records/warranty on the job card; re-test the set in the customer's presence where possible; identify the fault and explain it simply; repair free of charge if under warranty or agree on fair terms; follow up to confirm satisfaction
questions.explanation: Good relations retain customers, bring referrals and build reputation. Telephone: answer promptly, identify yourself, speak clearly, take notes, end politely. For a repeat fault: listen, apologise, check records and warranty, test and explain, repair free if under warranty, follow up.
